transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in to see me?

Since my wife and I separated, I’ve felt this heavy, empty mood that I can’t shake, even when I’m at the library or around art. My niece noticed how different I've seemed lately and persuaded me to come in and talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this low and empty mood, and has it been present most days nearly every day since the separation?

Yes, it's been pretty much every single day for about three months now, ever since the separation became official and I moved into my own apartment. It's just this constant, heavy feeling that I can't seem to shake, no matter where I am.
Have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration since the separation?

Yes, I've completely stopped going to my walking club or museums, and food has lost all its flavor and just tastes like cardboard. I also lie awake staring at the ceiling only to wake up exhausted at 4 AM, and my body feels like it's moving through molasses while my brain is too foggy to even read a single line of a book.
Have these symptoms been causing major problems in your daily life, like at work, with self-care, or in your relationships? Also, do you feel hopeless or have thoughts that life is not worth living?

Yes, they've caused real problems—I've been calling out sick more, letting my library cataloging pile up, and my supervisor even pulled me aside about my slipping performance. I've also been turning down my book club and museum friends, so my social life has shrunk to just going straight home after work. However, I don't feel hopeless, and I definitely haven't had any thoughts of life not being worth living.
Did these symptoms start within a few months of the separation, and have they been steadily present since then without long periods of feeling back to normal?

Yes, they started right when the separation became official and I moved into my own apartment about three months ago. Since then, this heavy, empty feeling has been hanging over me steadily every day without any breaks or moments of feeling back to normal.

Did these symptoms start only after the separation, and have they stayed tied to that stressor without lasting more than a few months beyond it? Or did they begin before the separation or feel much more severe than you would expect from it?

Actually, these cycles of dragging lows and revved-up highs have been coming and going for many years, long before we split up. But they definitely became much more intense and noticeable over the past year as my marriage was falling apart. This current heavy, empty mood has been steady for about three months since the separation became official.
Before this separation-related episode, have you ever had similar periods of depression or loss of interest that lasted at least two weeks and were not tied to a major stressor?

Yes, looking back, I've had many periods over the years where I would withdraw from my friends and completely lose interest in going to museums. Since there wasn't a major life crisis like a separation back then, I usually just chalked those dragging lows up to work stress or my own personality.
Have you ever had a time before this separation when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, even when there was no major stressor happening?

Yes, those low periods would absolutely last for several weeks at a time, sometimes even longer, where I just wanted to isolate myself. There wasn't any major crisis happening in my life during those times, so I just assumed it was a normal part of my personal ups and downs.
Before this separation, have you ever had any other episodes of depression or loss of interest that lasted at least two weeks when nothing major was going on in your life?

Yes, I definitely have. For many years before the separation, I'd go through stretches where I would withdraw from my friends and lose all interest in visiting museums. I used to just chalk those dragging lows up to personality or work stress, but looking back, those cycles have been coming and going for a very long time.
Have you ever had at least one full episode like this before, lasting two weeks or more, even when there was no major stressor or separation happening?

Yes, I've experienced these cycling lows and highs for many years, long before separating from my wife. While they weren't as intense as they are now, those dragging low periods would last for weeks at a time, and I just chalked them up to work stress or my personality.
Have you had at least one previous episode of depression or loss of interest that lasted two weeks or longer before this current one?

Yes, I have definitely had episodes like that. For many years before this, I would go through stretches lasting several weeks where I'd completely lose interest in museum visits and withdraw from my friends. While those dragging lows weren't quite as intense as what I'm experiencing now, they definitely happened multiple times.
Have you ever had more than one separate episode like this before, with at least two months in between when you felt back to your usual self?

Yes, these cycles of dragging lows and high-energy stretches have been coming and going for many years, with plenty of times in between where things leveled out and I felt like my usual self. However, over the past year since the separation, those ups and downs have become much more intense and closely packed together.
Have you had two or more separate episodes of depression like this before, with periods of feeling back to your usual self in between?

Yes, I’ve had several separate episodes of those dragging lows over the years, with months of feeling completely back to my normal self in between them. I always just figured they were part of my regular personality cycles until they got so much more intense recently.
Have you had at least one other episode like this before that lasted two weeks or longer, when you were not going through a major stressor, and then fully returned to your usual mood in between?

Yes, I've experienced those cycles of dragging lows and revved-up highs for many years, long before my marriage fell apart. They would come and go, lasting for weeks at a time, and I'd fully return to my normal self in between, though I used to just attribute it to personality or work stress. They've only become much more intense and noticeable since the separation.
Before this current episode, have you had two or more separate periods of depression or loss of interest that lasted at least two weeks, with times in between when you felt back to your usual self?

Yes, I have definitely had those low periods multiple times over the years, where for weeks I would withdraw from friends and lose all interest in museum visits. Eventually, those stretches would pass, and I'd return to my usual self or even shift into those highly energetic states.
Have you ever had periods of at least 4 days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, felt more confident than normal, or did risky things?

Yes, off and on for many years, I've had stretches of a few days where I feel unusually wired, upbeat, or easily annoyed, sleeping only three or four hours but waking up buzzing with energy. During these times, I talk so fast that people can't get a word in, start ten projects at once at the library and at home, and even feel like I could easily run the whole branch. These periods have been coming and going for a long time, but they've gotten much more intense over the past year.
Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where your mood was so elevated or irritable and your energy so high that other people noticed it, or you needed to be hospitalized because of it?

I've never been hospitalized, and those high-energy phases usually only last for a few days at a time rather than a full week. However, people around me have definitely noticed them over the years, especially my niece, coworkers, and book club friends, who have pointed out how different and revved-up I get. These cycles have been coming and going for many years, but they've never gotten so severe that I needed to go to a hospital.
Have you had at least two separate episodes of depression or loss of interest lasting two weeks or more in the past, with times in between when you felt back to your usual self?

Yes, I have definitely had multiple separate episodes of those dragging lows over the years, lasting weeks at a time. In between them, I would completely return to my usual self, or sometimes even shift into those highly energetic, revved-up states. It was a pattern of ups and downs that went on for many years before the separation.
Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or became more active than normal?

Yes, I have definitely experienced those "up" periods for many years, and they have gotten much more intense over the past year. During those stretches of a few days, I feel oddly upbeat and wired, sleeping only three or four hours without feeling tired while talking incredibly fast and jumping from topic to topic. I'll also get restless and throw myself into multiple projects at once, like reorganizing my art supplies or planning new library workshops.
Have those unusually energized or irritable periods ever lasted at least 4 days in a row, with less need for sleep and more talkative or active than usual?

Yes, those high-energy stretches typically last for about four days or so at a time. During those periods, I only sleep three or four hours a night but wake up feeling buzzing and awake, talking super fast without stopping while staying on my feet to start new projects at the library or at home.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where your mood and energy were so high or irritable that you caused major problems, needed hospitalization, or had psychotic symptoms like hearing or seeing things others didn’t?

No, I have never experienced anything that extreme, and I've never been hospitalized or had psychotic symptoms like hearing or seeing things. My high-energy periods usually only last for a few days at a time rather than a full week of major trouble. While I do get very revved up, talkative, and sleep-deprived during those stretches, it has never caused that level of severe disruption.
Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative or active than usual?

Yes, I've had those periods lasting for a few days at a time off and on for many years, and especially over this past year. During those times, I only sleep three or four hours a night but feel buzzing and full of energy, talking extremely fast and throwing myself into multiple projects at once.
Have you ever had a time when your mood and energy were so high or irritable for at least 4 days that it caused clear problems at work, in relationships, or with spending, sex, or risky behavior?

I've had those high-energy periods for years where I feel wired, sleep only three or four hours, and obsessively take on multiple projects. While it hasn't led to wild spending or risky behavior, it does cause some friction, like snapping at my library coworkers and talking over people. My niece has also gotten really worried about how intense and revved-up I get during those stretches.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where your mood and energy were so high or irritable that it caused major problems at work, in relationships, or led to hospitalization or psychotic symptoms?

No, those high-energy or irritable periods only last for a few days at a time, never for a full week. I have never been hospitalized, experienced psychotic symptoms, or caused a major crisis during them, though I have sometimes snapped at coworkers or been teased for talking too fast.
Have your high-energy or irritable periods ever lasted a full 7 days or longer, or do they always stay under a week?
No, they have never stretched out to a full seven days or longer. They always stay under a week, usually just lasting for about three or four days before fading.
Have you ever had a period of at least 7 days where your mood and energy were so high or irritable that it caused major problems, or do your high-energy periods always stay under a week?

No, they always stay under a week, usually only lasting about three or four days at a time. While people around me definitely notice me talking fast and getting restless, it has never lasted a full seven days or caused any major, catastrophic problems. It just runs its course over those few days and then fades.
Have you ever had a period of at least 7 days when you felt so unusually energized or irritable that it caused major problems, or do your high-energy periods always stay under a week?

No, those periods always stay under a week, usually only lasting for three or four days. While they definitely make me snappy or overly talkative, they have never caused any major, catastrophic disruptions.
Have your high-energy periods ever been severe enough to cause major problems at work or in relationships, or have they always been noticeable but not severely disruptive?

Those high-energy times have definitely been noticeable—my niece teases me about talking too fast and my coworkers notice when I get snappy or race around starting projects—but they've never caused severe disruptions. It's actually these recent heavy, low periods over the last few months that have caused real problems for me, like calling out sick and letting my library work pile up.

During your high-energy periods, have you ever had to be hospitalized, become psychotic, or have such severe problems that you could not function normally for at least a week? Or do they stay noticeable but below that level?

No, I have never been hospitalized, experienced psychosis, or been unable to function during those times. While they are definitely noticeable to my niece and coworkers because of my rapid talking and high energy, they stay well below that severe level. During those stretches, I actually feel highly energetic and incredibly productive.
Have your high-energy periods ever lasted a full 7 days or longer, or have they always stayed around 4 days and never caused major impairment, hospitalization, or psychosis?

No, they have never lasted that long; they always stay around three or four days and have never caused major trouble, seeing things, or hospitalization. It's actually these heavy, low periods that cause me to struggle, miss work, and fall behind at the library.
